intro.title: Sudoku Solver
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a Sudoku solver program that can automatically fill in a 9x9 puzzle grid while following the rules of Sudoku. You will learn the core concept of backtracking, a recursive algorithm that tries possible numbers in empty cells and undoes choices that lead to dead ends. The implementation will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like arrays, loops, conditionals, and functions. By the end, you'll understand how to apply algorithmic thinking to solve constraint-based problems step by step.
intro.usecase: Sudoku solvers demonstrate constraint satisfaction problems, a pattern used in real-world scheduling and resource allocation systems. For example, airline crew scheduling dashboards use similar backtracking algorithms to assign flights while respecting legal limits and availability. Calendar optimization tools in productivity apps apply these techniques to find meeting times that satisfy all participants' constraints. Even game development uses these algorithms for procedural level generation in puzzle games, ensuring solvable layouts.
